$comment: Every distribution in this repository that declares a version nobody can
install, with the reason that state is acceptable. Measured by
`scripts/declared_publication_sweep.py`, guarded by
`tests/architecture/test_declared_publication.py`.
## Why this file exists at all
`test_module_version_sync.py` proves a module's three version surfaces
AGREE. It cannot prove the agreed version EXISTS. `dotmac-integration`
reads 0.1.0a2 on all three surfaces and the version-identity guard passes,
while the newest tag is dotmac-integration-v0.1.0a1 — internal consistency
and publication are different questions, and only the first one had a
guard. A consumer reading the repository, the changelog or
docs/MODULE_CATALOG.md and pinning ==0.1.0a2 gets a resolver error.
## What a row here does and does not mean
A row means the state is KNOWN and someone has said why. It is not
permission to leave it there, and it is emphatically not a reason to edit
the declared version down to match the index: that would make the
repository agree with the registry by discarding the work the number
describes, and the changelog entry for the unpublished version would then
belong to nothing.
The repair is not always a release, either. `dotmac-imports` was reported
as an anomaly BECAUSE it was release-allowlisted with no tag; the ruling
was that the allowlist row was the wrong half, and it was removed rather
than the module published. Two states this file must keep distinct:
* INTENDED — the distribution is meant to be unpublished right now
(`dotmac-auth-oidc`, `dotmac-imports`). The row records the decision so
the next reader does not undo it by dispatching a release.
* OUTSTANDING — a version is genuinely owed to consumers. The row
records evidence a decision still needs. Two worked examples have now
passed through and been removed on release: `dotmac-integration`
0.1.0a2 (released as a3) and `dotmac-kernel` 0.1.0a67. A row that
expires on its own release is the healthiest shape an entry here has.
Both are recorded the same way and neither is a pass. The reason text is
where the difference lives, which is why the guard requires a premise
rather than a label.
## Two directions, both failures
A distribution entering this state without a row fails — that is a version
silently promised to consumers. A row whose distribution has since been
published ALSO fails and must be removed in the same change as the release,
because a ledger that only grows stops describing anything (ADR-0018).
## The oracle is a git tag
The release workflows write a tag only after `verify-registry` has
installed the exact published version from the private index and registered
its manifest, so a tag is this repository's own assertion that a version is
installable — stronger than 'an upload succeeded'. The index is not queried
directly: that needs an authenticated URL, which makes the check
un-runnable at PR time and offline, and a gate that cannot run is not a
gate. The stated cost is that a publication whose tag step failed reads
here as unpublished — which is exactly the state
`recover-module-release.yml` exists to repair, so reporting it is correct.

dotmac-app-sync.reason: INTENDED UNTIL A REAL PRODUCT PILOT. The provider-neutral contract, four flow proofs and architecture boundary are complete, but the stateless-adapter release lane deliberately requires one exact-SHA destination-owned receiver before publication. This package is therefore not allowlisted and cannot be dispatched. Remove this row only with the pilot evidence and the reviewed adapter-lane entry; do not treat its source tests as adoption or edit the declared version down.

dotmac-customers.reason: INTENDED FOR THE ADR-0055 BUILD COHORT, NOT RELEASED. The Sub-first account/profile boundary is audit-complete and uncomposed. Publishing is forbidden in this programme. Remove only with an authorized Sub backfill, zero-drift shadow and writer retirement.

dotmac-document-rendering.reason: INTENDED UNTIL THE BILLING DOCUMENT CUTOVER. This stateless package is built and gate-proven here but deliberately NOT release-allowlisted. Its kernel floor was corrected from an unpublished a87 to the published a88 in the #337 follow-up, so the floor resolves and the kernel is not what holds this row open; its EXTRACTION.toml withholds publication until Vendor Control Plane's Billing fact producer, the dotmac-files storage binding and the assembly-owned idempotent reconciler are ready in one cutover slice. No product is claimed as a consumer and no old writer is retired. Remove this row only in the reviewed publication and adoption sequence for the package itself; never by editing the declared version or floor down.

dotmac-fx-policy.reason: INTENDED FOR THE ADR-0055 BUILD COHORT, NOT RELEASED. The ERP-first FX observation and selection-policy owner is audit-complete and uncomposed; Money values, invoice snapshots, tax, provider I/O and GL consequences remain separate. Remove only with authorized ERP backfill, selection shadow and sealed writer retirement.

dotmac-imports.reason: RULED AND RESOLVED 2026-08-15: intended state, not a defect. The sweep first reported this as an anomaly because the module sat in .github/release-modules.json with no dotmac-imports-v tag in any version. The anomaly was the ALLOWLIST ROW, not the missing tag — the package's own EXTRACTION.toml next_action says to keep it audit-complete and unreleased until a real first adopter is ready, and to publish the exact kernel/imports releases just in time for that cutover. Michael ruled: remove the row, do NOT publish. The row is gone from release-modules.json, release-module.yml and recover-module-release.yml; the package keeps its declared 0.1.0a2, its catalogue entry, its kernel floor and its dossier. It is re-added with ERP's adoption proof (cutover 1, gated behind the E8 Organization-to-Tenant and composed-lineage decision). DO NOT 'fix' this by dispatching a release — unreleased is the decision.

dotmac-inbox-operations.reason: INTENDED FOR THE ADR-0055 BUILD COHORT, NOT RELEASED. The Sub/CRM-adjudicated staffed-inbox owner is audit-complete and uncomposed; a2 adds Sub's durable FIFO admission and round-robin rotation state (io_0002). Remove only with authorized Sub backfill/zero-drift cutover and verified CRM decision-copy retirement.

dotmac-kernel.reason: AUTHORIZED RELEASE CANDIDATE - NOT to be repaired by editing the version down. a93 allocates the two Cloud service-lifecycle lineages and installs no behaviour: domains/dn/mod_domains and hosting/hs/mod_hosting, authorized by the ADR-0030 amendment of 2026-08-23. domains does NOT take 'do': documents holds that prefix permanently, the dotmac-domains candidate tree still carries the stale provisional claim, and an allocation is never reused or repointed - so the row lands now while both modules are unreleased and a rename is still free. Neither module is on main at this version; both survive only on salvage/cloud-domains-hosting, so this allocates prefixes and claims nothing about implementation, review, testing, publication or adoption. Every published a85..a92 artifact carries neither row, so a93 is the floor for both. a92 is published and immutable, so new ledger rows need a new version. Remove this row after release-kernel registry verification writes the a93 tag - in the SAME change as the release, because a ledger that only ever grows stops describing anything.

dotmac-operational-escalations.reason: INTENDED FOR THE CUSTOMER-JOURNEY BUILD COHORT, NOT RELEASED. Versioned escalation policy, instances, acknowledgement and cancellation are extracted product-first from Sub's operational_escalation state and are uncomposed. Durable Timers keeps scheduling and Messaging/Integrator keeps delivery. Remove only with an authorized Sub backfill, zero-drift escalation shadow and writer retirement.

dotmac-payments.reason: INTENDED FOR THE CUSTOMER-JOURNEY BUILD COHORT, NOT RELEASED. Billing keeps receivables and settlement allocation, Banking keeps accounts, Integrator keeps provider transport. Remove only with an authorized Sub backfill, zero-drift correlation shadow and writer retirement.

dotmac-qualification.reason: INTENDED FOR THE ADR-0055 BUILD COHORT, NOT RELEASED. The Sub-first evidence/decision owner is audit-complete and uncomposed; positioning and Network Access remain observation sources. Remove only with authorized Sub backfill, zero-drift shadow and writer retirement.

dotmac-sales.reason: INTENDED UNTIL THE FIRST SUB ADOPTION. The accepted-quote owner is audit-complete and uncomposed: the assembly does not install it, and it is deliberately absent from the release allowlist. Its kernel floor is 0.1.0a88 — `sales` won the three-way `sa` arbitration in #321 and the row entered kernel source at a87, which was never dispatched, so a88 is the first installable kernel that can register the lineage. THE KERNEL IS NOT WHAT HOLDS THIS ROW OPEN; adoption is. Publishing before Sub's backfill and shadow would put an installable sales owner beside a product still writing its own quotes. Remove this row in the release change that adds the allowlist entry and records the Sub adoption; never by editing the declared version or the floor down.

dotmac-template-studio.reason: Not in any release lane — absent from release-modules.json and release-adapters.json alike — so no workflow can publish it and no consumer can pin it. It is the still-unlisted stand-in the allowlist gate's own sensitivity proof uses (`test_an_unallowlisted_package_cannot_be_resolved`), which makes unpublished the consistent state rather than an oversight. It is recorded rather than exempted because 0.2.0a3 is the third declared version of a package that has never had a first release.

dotmac-fulfillment.reason: INTENDED UNTIL THE FIRST PARTICIPANT ADAPTER. This package owns the fulfillment saga — runs, steps, participant attempts, outcome receipts, compensation and convergence — as a tenant-only module with FORCEd RLS and append-only evidence, built and gate-proven here. Its floor is kernel 0.1.0a89: a86 minted the mod_fulfillment lineage, but the package also consumes the typed provisioning participant, scoped request, asynchronous outcome envelope and participant-decided compensation contract that land in a89, and the highest consumed capability wins. a89 is published, registry-verified and tagged, so unlike the earlier a86 reading this floor is one an installer can resolve. THE KERNEL IS THEREFORE NO LONGER WHAT HOLDS THIS ROW OPEN. What holds it open is adoption: it is deliberately NOT release-allowlisted until the released dotmac-durable-timers dependency is composed and the first Dotmac Cloud participant adapter exists. Package supply alone is not adoption, and publishing before a named participant would put an installable saga owner beside products that still drive their own — the failure the imports row above was ruled on. Remove this row only in the release change that adds the allowlist entry and records that first participant; never by editing the declared version down.
